home.programsTitle: Clear information, in person and at no cost
home.programsLead: Each event combines a short talk, time for questions, and one-on-one consultations with volunteers. We work on four fronts.

programs.title: Immigration guidance
programs.body: The paths to obtaining status, explained one by one: asylum, TPS, family petitions, work visas, and more. What each one requires and how long it usually takes.

programs.title: Navigating the system
programs.body: The everyday things no one explains: opening a bank account, enrolling your children in school, getting a driver's license, filing taxes, and using the health care system.

programs.title: Know your rights
programs.body: What you can do and what you don't have to do when dealing with the authorities, how to spot fraud, and where to turn if something goes wrong.

programs.title: Consultations with volunteers
programs.body: At the end of each event, lawyers and paralegals answer individual questions, first come, first served. No appointment and no cost.

home.programsCaption: Every event ends with one-on-one consultations
home.eventsLead: In person, in Spanish, and open to the whole family. Reserving guarantees your printed guide.
home.stepsTitle: What a Fundación Verde event is like

steps.title: Register at no cost
steps.body: Choose the event and leave your name and how many people are coming with you. You'll get a confirmation by WhatsApp or email.

steps.title: Arrive and get your guide
steps.body: We'll be waiting with a printed guide on the day's topic. You don't need to bring documents.

steps.title: Listen and ask
steps.body: A 45-minute talk in Spanish, followed by open questions.

steps.title: Talk with a volunteer
steps.body: Brief one-on-one consultations, first come, first served, to give guidance on your specific case.

home.promiseTitle: Four things that don't happen at our events
promises: No one charges you for entry, for the guide, or for the consultation.
No one asks for your immigration status to take part.
No one promises you an outcome or sells you a service.
No one who isn't a licensed lawyer gives you legal guidance.
home.giveTitle: Your contribution keeps the events free
home.giveLead: Every event means printing guides, renting a room, paying interpreters, and offering coffee. Volunteers give their time; your donation covers the rest.

impacts.label: An interpreter for an entire session
The room rental for one event

home.questionsLead: Some of the most common ones. Each event answers the ones on its topic and leaves time for yours.

questions.q: Can I petition for my mom if I already have a green card?
My TPS expires this year. What are my options?
Do I need a lawyer to apply for asylum, or can I do it on my own?
Can I open a bank account without a Social Security number?
How do I file taxes if I don't have status yet?
If the police stop me, do I have to say where I'm from?

home.teaserTitle: We were founded to give back to the immigrant community
home.teaserBody: Fundación Verde is the Verde family's social initiative. We work alongside Verde Law, the firm that provides volunteer lawyers, so that the information that changes a family's direction doesn't depend on being able to pay for a consultation.

mision.title: A family foundation that gives back to the immigrant community
mision.lead: We believe clear information changes a family's direction. That's why we offer it in person, in Spanish, and at no cost.
why: Every day, people come to Verde Law who have spent years in the country without knowing they had an option, or who spent their savings on someone who wasn't a lawyer. Most of those stories began with a lack of information.

Fundación Verde was born from the Verde family to change that starting point. We host in-person events where volunteer lawyers and specialists explain, without fine print, how to obtain status and how the system works in the United States.
We don't sell anything at our events. Entry is free, consultations are free, and no one is obligated to hire a service.

values.title: Clarity
values.body: We explain with examples and in people's own language. If it isn't understood, it doesn't help.

values.title: Free of charge
values.body: No Foundation event, guide, or consultation has a cost. Ever.

values.title: Responsibility
values.body: The information comes from licensed lawyers and trained volunteers. No rumors.

values.title: Closeness
values.body: We go where people already gather: churches, schools, libraries, and community centers.

programas.title: Four fronts, one goal: that you understand your options
programas.lead: All programs are delivered at in-person events, in Spanish, with printed material and one-on-one consultations at the end.

blocks.title: Immigration guidance
blocks.body: We explain the paths to obtaining status, what each one requires, and how long it usually takes. No promised outcomes and no jargon: the goal is for you to leave knowing what your path could be and what to ask when you look for representation.

blocks.title: Navigating the system
blocks.body: The everyday things no one explains when you arrive: how to open a bank account, enroll your children in school, get a driver's license, file taxes with an ITIN, or access health services. Each session invites a specialist on the topic.

blocks.title: Know your rights
blocks.body: What you can do and what you don't have to do when dealing with the authorities, how to recognize a fake lawyer or notario, and where to turn if something goes wrong. Responsible information, shared calmly, so decisions aren't made out of fear.

blocks.title: Consultations with volunteers
blocks.body: At the end of each event, volunteer lawyers and paralegals answer individual questions, first come, first served, about ten minutes per person. You don't need to bring documents: just describe your situation to receive initial guidance and learn what the next step is.

p: When you reserve a spot, subscribe to the newsletter, or write to us, we collect the information you give us: name, email, WhatsApp number, city, and the message you send. We do not ask for your immigration status.
We use this information to confirm your reservation, notify you of upcoming events if you asked us to, reply to your message, and prepare enough guides and chairs.
We do not sell your data. We store it in tools that help us manage reservations, messages, and donations, such as our contact system and payment platform.
You can ask us to correct or delete your data, or stop receiving notices at any time, by writing to hola@fundacionverde.org.
The content of this site and of our events is general and educational. It does not replace legal advice about your case or create an attorney-client relationship.
Reserving a spot is free and doesn't commit you to anything. Spots are limited and venues may change; we'll let you know by WhatsApp or email if that happens.
Donations are processed securely through our payment platform. You can cancel a monthly donation whenever you want.
If you have questions about these terms, write to us at hola@fundacionverde.org.
